Window ids in the key: ip-auth, auth-fail, code-email-1h, code-email-1d, person; code-email counts both windows and the wait is the longest refusing one. A refused event is counted too. SF-143: the Counter port has only incr, so a failure limit can be checked only by counting: the 6th failure in a window is refused, but nothing can ask 'is this email+prefix already over?' before a sign-in attempt without counting. SF-144: the posted answer is powSalt, powN, powSig only, so the salt carries its own expiry: <16 random bytes base64url>.<expires epoch ms>; sig = hex HMAC-SHA256(HMAC secret, 'pow:' + challenge) with challenge = hex SHA-256(salt + n), so the signature binds salt, expiry and n. The 'pow:' prefix separates it from the counter-key HMACs under the same stage secret (D-115). createPow({ powStore, clock, secretStore, settings, max? }) exports issue() -> { salt, challenge, max, expires, sig } and verify({ salt, n, sig }) -> { ok: true } | { ok: false, reason: 'missing' | 'malformed' | 'wrong' | 'expired' | 'reused' }; checks run shape, signature (timingSafeEqual), expiry, then the claim, so a wrong or stale answer writes no row. n must be a decimal string 0..max. The claim is POW#<hex sha256 of salt> for 10 minutes from the claim (it outlives the answer); DynamoPowStore puts with 'attribute_not_exists(pk) OR expires_at <= :now' so a row past expires_at whose TTL lags can be claimed again (the answer is already expired by then).

SF-144: the brief says PowField takes the nonce from x-nonce, but the solver awaits crypto.subtle.digest on the main thread and renders only three hidden inputs: no worker, inline script or style, so there is nothing to put a nonce on and PowField takes none (a Worker would be blocked anyway under script-src 'strict-dynamic', which ignores 'self'). The fetch to /api/auth/pow is same-origin (connect-src 'self'). PowField re-solves after each submit and 9 minutes after its fetch (timed from the fetch, not from expires, so a skewed device clock cannot loop), and marks the salt input data-state solving|ready for SF-153's browser tests. The Origin and proof-of-work refusals log no security event (Contracts lists none for them); the ip-auth refusal logs rate_limited with outcome ip-auth. An unexpected failure is not logged either (no event in the Contracts list fits); SF-148 on may want one.
